name: Dabrafenib + Trametinib for BRAF V600E Anaplastic Thyroid Carcinoma
cyclesNote: continuous until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; not a fixed cycle count

source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: This BRAF-directed doublet is gated to BRAF V600E-mutated anaplastic thyroid carcinoma. NCCN recommends molecular testing (including BRAF, with BRAF IHC for faster turnaround) to inform systemic therapy. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Thyroid Carcinoma v2.2026, Anaplastic Carcinoma (ANAP) and Discussion MS-39.

supportiveCare: monitor for pyrexia (common with dabrafenib/trametinib), cutaneous toxicity and secondary skin neoplasms, ocular events, LVEF decline, and hyperglycemia per labeling.
consider hepatitis B screening prior to systemic therapy per the thyroid systemic therapy principles (THYR-B footnote a).
monitoring: clinical and cross-sectional imaging (CT or MRI with contrast) response assessment
dermatologic surveillance for secondary cutaneous neoplasms

doseModificationRules.text: Interrupt and manage per labeling; resume at a reduced dose if indicated; obtain clinical review.
Hold and obtain cardiology review before continuation.

drugs.name: Dabrafenib
drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Thyroid Carcinoma v2.2026, Discussion MS-39. Dabrafenib 150 mg PO TWICE DAILY (represented as continuous daily dosing; twice-daily frequency is source-stated). BRAF V600E gate required. Given continuously until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

provenance.locator: Discussion MS-39 (dabrafenib 150 mg, twice daily, in combination with trametinib 2 mg once daily, in BRAF V600E-mutated ATC)

drugs.name: Trametinib
drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Thyroid Carcinoma v2.2026, Discussion MS-39. Trametinib 2 mg PO ONCE DAILY, combined with dabrafenib. MEK inhibitor added to the BRAF inhibitor. Given continuously until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

provenance.locator: Discussion MS-39 (trametinib 2 mg once daily in combination with dabrafenib 150 mg twice daily, BRAF V600E-mutated ATC)
